blocks.text: Winning a court case (second or third century ad):
omnia recte se habent. quomodo te habes?
blocks.speaker: gaius

blocks.text: gratulor tibi sicut mihi. sed iudicium habeo.
blocks.speaker: lucius

blocks.text: non valde magnum; est enim pecuniarium, ut omne videas. si vacat tibi, veni nobiscum; iudices diem nobis dederunt, quae hodie est, et sententia dicetur. quare volo te praesente de causa cum advocatis tractare.
blocks.speaker: lucius

blocks.text: bene fecisti. constituistine? circa quam horam? in quo loco?
blocks.speaker: gaius

blocks.text: in foro, in porticu, iuxta stoam Victoriae.
blocks.speaker: lucius

blocks.text: sed rogo ut hoc in mente habeas.
blocks.speaker: lucius

blocks.text: securus esto; mihi pertinet. l u c i u s (to son): eamus nos ad nummularium; accipiamus ab eo denarios centum; demus eos causidico et advocatis et iuris peritis, ut quam optime defendant nos. hic est. accipe ab eo denarios et sequere. (on arrival at court) sicut constituimus, adest Gaius. convocemus eum in consilium. hic habemus instrumenta.
blocks.speaker: gaius

blocks.text: testatus sum. tacete, audiamus sententiam. audivistine nos vicisse, Gai?
blocks.speaker: lucius

rows: habeō with a reflexive is equivalent to ‘be’
ad (+ accusative) ‘before’ (i.e. in the court of)
vacat tibi ‘you have leisure’ (literally ‘it is vacant to you’)
iūris perītus, iūris perītī (m.) ‘legal expert’ (literally ‘skilled in law’)
diēs, diēī (f.) ‘appointed date’ (note gender in this meaning!)

blocks.text: Very badly: I must go to the forum today to help my friend Marcus.
blocks.speaker: gaius

blocks.text: He has a court case before the quaestor, since he owes many denarii.
blocks.speaker: gaius

blocks.text: But Marcus bought a new house yesterday.
blocks.speaker: lucius

blocks.text: He did (Latin ‘he bought’), although he has no money, and now that house will have to be given to his creditors, provided that the judge is wise. But I must not say such things, for he is my friend. When he loses his house, he will have to live with me.
blocks.speaker: gaius

blocks.text: You are a good friend; therefore it is fitting for you to be praised. Additional Vocabulary dēbeō, dēbēre, dēbuī, dēbitum ‘owe’ crēditor, crēditōris (m.) ‘creditor’ habitō, -āre, -āvī, -ātum ‘live’ (in the sense of ‘dwell’; vīvō means ‘be alive’)
blocks.speaker: lucius

blocks.text: Juno visits the god of the winds (continuation of the passage in chapter 42):

Talia flammato secum dea corde volutans nimborum in patriam, loca feta furentibus Austris, Aeoliam venit. hic vasto rex Aeolus antro luctantis ventos tempestatesque sonoras imperio premit ac vinclis et carcere frenat. illi indignantes magno cum murmure montis circum claustra fremunt; celsa sedet Aeolus arce sceptra tenens mollitque animos et temperat iras; ni faciat, maria ac terras caelumque profundum quippe ferant rapidi secum verrantque per auras.

rows: Aeolia, Aeoliae (f.) name of a place
Aeolus, Aeolī (m.) name of the god of the winds
A possible prose order of the above would be:
Talia flammato corde secum volutans dea in patriam nimborum, loca feta furentibus Austris,

Aeoliam venit. hic vasto antro rex Aeolus ventos luctantis tempestatesque sonoras imperio premit ac vinclis et carcere frenat. illi indignantes cum magno murmure circum claustra montis fremunt; celsa arce sedet Aeolus sceptra tenens mollitque animos et iras temperat; ni faciat, maria ac terras caelumque profundum quippe rapidi secum ferant perque auras verrant.
